old_evidence.text: You can’t reuse EPS *PaymentMethods* (PaymentMethods represent your customer's payment instruments, used with the Payment Intents or Setup Intents APIs) or save them to customers.

findings: New raw lines 5-18 contain only an EPS purpose sentence and five variant links. Diff lines 3-17 and 1624-1629 show the older body replaced by an index in this root capture; no behavioral removal or renewal of detailed examples is established. Source lines 4-7 and 40-42 currently cite only the May 3, 2026 raw and need separate November index provenance.

The May guide says EPS is single-use, requires bank authentication/redirect, and must follow EPS terms (old raw lines 26-28). Checkout supports EUR payment mode only, with one-time EUR line items and no setup/subscription mode (old raw lines 30-47); hosted success_url and embedded return_url are distinct (old raw lines 69-112). Source lines 13, 19 summarize core restrictions but omit terms, supported business locations and same-currency one-time line-item conditions.

Source line 13 says EPS requires customer name in billing details without a UI qualifier. The old mobile variants collect a name (old raw lines 267-306, 472-480, 678-720) and legacy Elements requires accountholder name (old raw lines 979-1003, 1129-1156), but hosted Checkout instructions at old raw lines 49-121 do not impose a manual name-field instruction. Qualify this by path rather than assert all-path requirement.

The legacy Elements route explicitly says epsBank is no longer available in latest Stripe.js and recommends Payment Element (old raw lines 830-835, 970-973). It also documents an optional server-side manual redirect with requires_action/redirect_to_url (old raw lines 1447-1540). Source lines 35-38 correctly label legacy and single-use but do not surface manual redirect or its pending outcome boundary.

Old raw lines 332-336, 532-536, 742-746 and 1391-1401 distinguish payment_intent.succeeded event from client callback and test-only requires_action transitions; return_url query parameters at old raw lines 1330-1340 enable status retrieval, not proof of payment. The JSON examples include source/Charge status pending at old raw lines 1343-1388 and 1475-1528, which must not be promoted as a successful live result.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain May 3, 2026 EPS payment-mode, EUR and one-time Checkout conditions, supported business locations, terms, refund/no-dispute claims (old raw lines 26-47, 123-127).

Retain dated iOS, Android, React Native and legacy Elements implementation examples with server PaymentIntent/client secret separation, manual redirect option, deep links and Stripe.js/SDK version context (old raw lines 231-336, 430-536, 636-746, 768-835, 953-973, 1129-1156, 1447-1544).
Keep the May test-only success/failure status transitions, 27-bank value table and single-use PaymentMethod limit as dated evidence (old raw lines 1391-1395, 1542-1544, 1593-1623).
conflicts: Source line 13 implies a universal customer-name billing requirement; old raw lines 49-121 give no such manual Checkout instruction, while old raw lines 267-306, 472-480, 678-720 and 979-1003 explicitly require collecting it in native/legacy Elements paths. Scope the summary by UI; wiki/concepts/stripe-eps.md lines 34-40 already does so.
unresolved_questions: The five November variant URLs at new raw lines 13-18 are links only in the pinned packet; November details, current SDK support, latest bank list and whether the linked Elements variant remains legacy are unverified.

findings: Add the November root-index raw reference while retaining the May detailed guide and its date (source lines 4-7, 40-42; new raw lines 9-18).
Qualify source line 13's name requirement to native and legacy Elements input; Checkout's old raw lines 49-121 do not state a manual name-field requirement.

Preserve Checkout EUR/one-time conditions and terms (old raw lines 26-47), legacy-only epsBank warning (old raw lines 830-835, 970-973), and event-versus-browser-return boundary (old raw lines 1330-1401).

source_assessments.reason: The new raw changes navigation only, but a new raw citation and a path-specific baseline accuracy correction are needed; old detailed claims remain dated rather than superseded.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/eps/accept-a-payment, the complete November capture (new raw lines 5-18) says EPS is an Austrian payment method and links Checkout, Elements, iOS, Android and React Native variants; it establishes no current API prerequisites, state transitions or successful outcome. The May guide (old raw lines 26-47, 49-112, 231-248, 1129-1156, 1391-1401, 1542-1544) documents EPS terms, EUR and one-time Checkout payment mode, a server Checkout Session or PaymentIntent, client secret and bank redirect authentication, success/failure event boundaries, and single-use PaymentMethods. source-stripe-eps-accept-payment.md captures the routes and legacy caveat but its line 13 overgeneralizes manually collected billing name across hosted Checkout.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/eps/accept-a-payment, the captured change is navigation/presentation: the May full guide (old raw lines 8-1623) became a five-variant root index (new raw lines 9-18), with no substantive behavioral replacement proven. source-stripe-eps-accept-payment.md should add November provenance while retaining May-dated EUR, Checkout line-item, legacy Elements, mobile SDK, optional manual redirect and 27-bank claims. Its name-field statement at source line 13 needs a UI qualification because old raw lines 49-121 do not require manual hosted Checkout collection while old raw lines 267-306 and 979-1003 do for native/legacy Elements. Account v2 preview wording, Stripe.js dahlia, SDK examples and test states remain dated; PaymentIntent creation, bank return, or a pending sample Charge is not payment success, which the older guide ties to payment_intent.succeeded (old raw lines 1330-1401).
